tegünčilen kü bügüde : tendeče basa
burqan-u gegen beye qotala-a
ilete üjegden bütübei ::
mön tegünčilen kü bügüde : tendeče basa
jirγalang ba gegen bayasqulang :
neretü samadi olbai : tendeče
basa burqan-u gegen
gerel-ün čoγ küčün bügüdeger-i :
sayitur todoraγulun bügüdeger-ün
činar anu : yambar kemebesü
tegünčilen iregsen-ü gegen
oron ba jokiyal kiged
niγuča ba orošiγsan kiged
čaγ ba oron kiged
buyan-u činar mön tegünčilen kü
bügüde : tendeče basa burqan-u
gegen beye gerel bügüdeger-i
ilete üjegülküi neretü
samadi olbai : tere kü
samadi-yin küčün-iyer burqan-u
gegen beye mön tegünčilen
kü bügüde : tendeče basa
burqan-u : gegen gerel-ün

ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠨᠴᠢᠯᠡᠨ ᠬᠦ ᠪᠦᠭᠦᠳᠡ ∶ ᠲᠡᠨᠳᠡᠴᠡ ᠪᠠᠰᠠ
ᠪᠤᠷᠬᠠᠨ ᠤ ᠭᠡᠭᠡᠨ ᠪᠡᠶ᠎ᠡ ᠬᠣᠲᠠᠯᠠ ᠠ
ᠢᠯᠡᠲᠡ ᠦᠵᠡᠭᠳᠡᠨ ᠪᠦᠲᠦᠪᠡᠢ ∷
ᠮᠥᠨ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠨᠴᠢᠯᠡᠨ ᠬᠦ ᠪᠦᠭᠦᠳᠡ ∶ ᠲᠡᠨᠳᠡᠴᠡ ᠪᠠᠰᠠ
ᠵᠢᠷᠭᠠᠯᠠᠩ ᠪᠠ ᠭᠡᠭᠡᠨ ᠪᠠᠶᠠᠰᠬᠤᠯᠠᠩ ∶
ᠨᠡᠷᠡᠲᠦ ᠰᠠᠮᠠᠳᠢ ᠣᠯᠪᠠᠢ ∶ ᠲᠡᠨᠳᠡᠴᠡ
ᠪᠠᠰᠠ ᠪᠤᠷᠬᠠᠨ ᠤ ᠭᠡᠭᠡᠨ
ᠭᠡᠷᠡᠯ ᠦᠨ ᠴᠣᠭ ᠬᠦᠴᠦᠨ ᠪᠦᠭᠦᠳᠡᠭᠡᠷ ᠢ ∶
ᠰᠠᠶᠢᠲᠤᠷ ᠲᠣᠳᠣᠷᠠᠭᠤᠯᠤᠨ ᠪᠦᠭᠦᠳᠡᠭᠡᠷ ᠦᠨ
ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠷ ᠠᠨᠤ ∶ ᠶᠠᠮᠪᠠᠷ ᠬᠡᠮᠡᠪᠡᠰᠦ
ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠨᠴᠢᠯᠡᠨ ᠢᠷᠡᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠦ ᠭᠡᠭᠡᠨ
ᠣᠷᠣᠨ ᠪᠠ ᠵᠣᠬᠢᠶᠠᠯ ᠬᠢᠭᠡᠳ ○
ᠨᠢᠭᠤᠴᠠ ᠪᠠ ᠣᠷᠣᠰᠢᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠬᠢᠭᠡᠳ
ᠴᠠᠭ ᠪᠠ ᠣᠷᠣᠨ ᠬᠢᠭᠡᠳ
ᠪᠤᠶᠠᠨ ᠤ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠷ ᠮᠥᠨ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠨᠴᠢᠯᠡᠨ ᠬᠦ
ᠪᠦᠭᠦᠳᠡ ∶ ᠲᠡᠨᠳᠡᠴᠡ ᠪᠠᠰᠠ ᠪᠤᠷᠬᠠᠨ ᠤ
ᠭᠡᠭᠡᠨ ᠪᠡᠶ᠎ᠡ ᠭᠡᠷᠡᠯ ᠪᠦᠭᠦᠳᠡᠭᠡᠷ ᠢ
ᠢᠯᠡᠲᠡ ᠦᠵᠡᠭᠦᠯᠬᠦᠢ ᠨᠡᠷᠡᠲᠦ
ᠰᠠᠮᠠᠳᠢ ᠣᠯᠪᠠᠢ ∶ ᠲᠡᠷᠡ ᠬᠦ
ᠰᠠᠮᠠᠳᠢ ᠶᠢᠨ ᠬᠦᠴᠦᠨ ᠢᠶᠡᠷ ᠪᠤᠷᠬᠠᠨ ᠤ
ᠭᠡᠭᠡᠨ ᠪᠡᠶ᠎ᠡ ᠮᠥᠨ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠨᠴᠢᠯᠡᠨ
ᠬᠦ ᠪᠦᠭᠦᠳᠡ ∶ ᠲᠡᠨᠳᠡᠴᠡ ᠪᠠᠰᠠ
ᠪᠤᠷᠬᠠᠨ ᠤ ∶ ᠭᠡᠭᠡᠨ ᠭᠡᠷᠡᠯ ᠦᠨ

<margin>Volume <term>ba</term> <gloss>fifteenth volume letter in the Kanjur</gloss>, Second Fascicle, Upper Part, Folio Two <note>original: "ba nögüge degedü qoyar / ᠪᠠ ᠨᠥᠭᠦᠭᠡ ᠳᠡᠭᠡᠳᠦ ᠬᠣᠶᠠᠷ"</note></margin>

in that very same way, all of them <note>original: "tegünčilen kü bügüde"; a standard sutra abbreviation formula indicating that the full series of qualities previously stated is to be repeated</note>. Thereupon, furthermore,
the <term>gegen beye</term> <gloss>radiant body</gloss> of the <term>burqan</term> <gloss>Buddha</gloss>, universally and to all,
was manifestly seen and accomplished.
<term>Mön tegünčilen kü bügüde</term> <gloss>All the rest is in that very same way</gloss>. Thereupon, furthermore,
known as "Bliss and Radiant Joy" <note>original: "jirγalang ba gegen bayasqulang"</note>,
that <term>samadi</term> <gloss>meditative absorption, Sanskrit samādhi</gloss> was attained. Thereupon,
furthermore, of the <term>burqan</term> <gloss>Buddha</gloss> and his <term>gegen gerel</term> <gloss>radiant light</gloss>,
all of its <term>čoγ küčün</term> <gloss>glorious powers</gloss>
being thoroughly illuminated, the nature of all of them:
if one asks what that nature is, namely,
it is the radiant realm of the <term>tegünčilen iregsen</term> <gloss>Thus-Come One, Sanskrit Tathāgata</gloss>
and his enlightened deeds <note>original: "jokiyal"</note>, as well as
his secret mysteries and his abiding state <note>original: "niγuča ba orošiγsan"</note>, as well as
the time and the place, as well as
the <term>buyan-u činar</term> <gloss>nature of merit</gloss>, and in that very same way
all the rest. Thereupon, furthermore, of the <term>burqan</term> <gloss>Buddha</gloss> and his
<term>gegen beye</term> <gloss>radiant body</gloss> and lights, all of them,
the absorption named "Manifestly Revealing" <note>original: "burqan-u gegen beye gerel bügüdeger-i ilete üjegülküi", meaning "Manifestly Revealing All the Radiant Bodies and Lights of the Buddha"</note>,
that <term>samadi</term> <gloss>meditative absorption</gloss> was attained. Through that very
<term>samadi</term>'s power, the <term>burqan</term> <gloss>Buddha</gloss> and his
<term>gegen beye</term> <gloss>radiant body</gloss> were manifested, and in that very same way
all the rest. Thereupon, furthermore,
of the <term>burqan</term> <gloss>Buddha</gloss> and his <term>gegen gerel</term> <gloss>radiant light</gloss> <meta>continues on next page</meta>

<summary>This folio from a red-ink Beijing woodblock print of the Mongolian Kanjur enumerates a sequence of Buddhist meditative absorptions, known as samadi, including "Bliss and Radiant Joy" and "Manifestly Revealing All the Radiant Bodies and Lights of the Buddha." Through these absorptions, the radiant body, glorious light, enlightened deeds, secret mysteries, and nature of merit of the Tathāgata are made manifest.</summary>
